125 F1.numberNote: Monaco GP 1950 (2nd, Ferrari's first World Championship race): #40, painted plain white on both sides of the tail, across the top of the tail and on the nose above the grille. Ascari also raced the 125 at the Swiss GP 1950 as #18.
125 F1.tobaccoNote: none - no tobacco (or any commercial) branding in this era; works Ferraris carried no sponsor decals on the bodywork. Tyre maker names appeared only on the tyre sidewalls. Pirelli tyres.
125 F1.notes: Plain dark rosso corsa, Borrani wire wheels with polished alloy rims, chrome eggcrate grille. Only a tiny yellow shield on the nose flank beside the grille.

275 F1.numberNote: Belgian GP 1950 at Spa (5th): #4, plain white on both sides of the tail, top of the tail and low on the nose sides. The 275 used the same body as the 125.
275 F1.tobaccoNote: none - no tobacco (or any commercial) branding in this era; works Ferraris carried no sponsor decals on the bodywork. Tyre maker names appeared only on the tyre sidewalls. Pirelli tyres.
275 F1.notes: Same look as the 125 F1: plain dark rosso corsa, wire wheels, no nose band.

stripes.note: blue identification band around the nose and grille surround at Monza 1951 (Ascari's colour, to match his blue helmet)

375 F1.numberNote: Chosen race: Italian GP 1951 at Monza, Ascari won as #2 (large white numbers on the tail sides and top, plus the nose sides and top). Other 1951 races: German GP win #71 (Nurburgring). 1950 Italian GP (secondary car): Ascari started #16, retired, then took over Serafini's #48 to finish 2nd.
375 F1.tobaccoNote: none - no tobacco (or any commercial) branding in this era; works Ferraris carried no sponsor decals on the bodywork. Tyre maker names appeared only on the tyre sidewalls. Pirelli tyres.
375 F1.notes: Ferrari used coloured nose bands on and off in 1951 to identify drivers (Ascari blue, Gonzalez yellow, Villoresi white, Taruffi green). There were no bands at the 1951 British GP.

stripes.note: pale blue ring around the nose air intake

375 Indianapolis.numberNote: Indianapolis 500 1952: #12, large white numbers on the nose sides and tail sides.
375 Indianapolis.tobaccoNote: none - no tobacco (or any commercial) branding in this era; works Ferraris carried no sponsor decals on the bodywork. Tyre maker names appeared only on the tyre sidewalls. Firestone tyres (Indy).
375 Indianapolis.notes: 'Ferrari Special' was the entry name, painted in white script on the bonnet/cowl sides. It is not a sponsor.

500 F2.numberNote: Ascari's main season is 1952. He won the German GP at the Nurburgring as #101 to clinch his first title (white numbers on the tail sides and top). Ascari 1952: French #8, British #15, German #101, Dutch #2, Italian #12. Ascari 1953: Argentine #10, French #10, British #5, Swiss #46 (clinched the title). Hawthorn 1953: won the French GP at Reims as #16 (white numbers painted straight on the nose top and the tail). At the British GP 1953 he was #8, with a black number on a white roundel on the nose (the British GP used roundels).
500 F2.tobaccoNote: none - no tobacco (or any commercial) branding in this era; works Ferraris carried no sponsor decals on the bodywork. Tyre maker names appeared only on the tyre sidewalls. Pirelli tyres.
500 F2.notes: Plain rosso corsa with no nose band at the chosen races. Yellow shield on the scuttle sides beside the cockpit.

625 F1.numberNote: Hawthorn's main season is 1954. He was 2nd in the Italian GP at Monza as #40 (white numbers painted straight on the nose sides and the tail). Ascari's one-off Ferrari drive at Monza 1954 was #34. Other Hawthorn 1954 races: British GP #11 (2nd, black-on-white roundels), Swiss GP #22. Hawthorn 1955 (secondary car): British GP at Aintree #16, shared with Castellotti, with black-on-white roundels on the nose.
625 F1.tobaccoNote: none - no tobacco (or any commercial) branding in this era; works Ferraris carried no sponsor decals on the bodywork. Tyre maker names appeared only on the tyre sidewalls. Pirelli tyres in 1954.
625 F1.notes: Plain rosso corsa. At the 1954 French GP the Ferraris had driver-colour noses (Hawthorn green), but Monza photos show no band.

553 F1.numberNote: Spanish GP 1954 at Pedralbes, Hawthorn won as #38: large white numbers straight on the nose sides and top and on the tail sides and top. Hawthorn also raced a 553 at the French GP 1954 as #6, reportedly with a green identification nose.
553 F1.tobaccoNote: none - no tobacco (or any commercial) branding in this era; works Ferraris carried no sponsor decals on the bodywork. Tyre maker names appeared only on the tyre sidewalls. Pirelli tyres.
553 F1.notes: Plain rosso corsa 'Squalo' with no nose band in Spain.

stripes.note: yellow identification nose tip

555 F1.numberNote: Dutch GP 1955 at Zandvoort, Hawthorn was 7th as #2: a black number on a white roundel on the tail sides and top. Italian GP 1955 at Monza: #6 (retired, gearbox; Englebert tyres by then).
555 F1.tobaccoNote: none - no tobacco (or any commercial) branding in this era; works Ferraris carried no sponsor decals on the bodywork. Tyre maker names appeared only on the tyre sidewalls. Pirelli tyres at Zandvoort; Englebert by Monza 1955.
555 F1.notes: The yellow nose and black #2 on white come from the Tecnomodel and Brumm replicas of this car. A forum post suggests Brumm's attribution might mix it up with Gonzalez's similar 1954 French GP 553, so treat it with care.

stripes.note: light blue nose tip (Argentine colours), German GP 1956
yellow band just behind the blue nose tip

D50.numberNote: Chosen race: German GP 1956 at the Nurburgring, Fangio won from pole as #1 in a long-nose car. A narrow white '1' was painted straight on the nose top and on the pannier sidepods. Fangio 1956: Argentine #34 (Musso's car, win), Monaco #20 then Collins's #26, Belgian #2, French #10, British #1 (win; black 1 on a white roundel, plain red nose), German #1 (win), Italian #22, then Collins's #26 (2nd, title clinched).
D50.tobaccoNote: none - no tobacco (or any commercial) branding in this era; works Ferraris carried no sponsor decals on the bodywork. Tyre maker names appeared only on the tyre sidewalls. Englebert tyres.
D50.notes: Lancia-Ferrari D50 with pannier fuel tanks between the wheels. Each race had different driver identification colours. The blue and yellow nose was specific to Fangio at the Nurburgring.

stripes.note: light blue identification nose band

801 F1.numberNote: German GP 1957 at the Nurburgring, Hawthorn was 2nd as #8: black numbers on white roundels on the nose top, tail sides and tail top. Other 1957 races: French #14 (4th), British #10 (3rd).
801 F1.tobaccoNote: none - no tobacco (or any commercial) branding in this era; works Ferraris carried no sponsor decals on the bodywork. Tyre maker names appeared only on the tyre sidewalls. Englebert tyres.
801 F1.notes: The light blue nose comes from the GP Replicas model of this car; contemporary black-and-white photos cannot confirm the colour. Collins's #7 sister car had a different nose.

246 F1.numberNote: Hawthorn won the 1958 title at the Moroccan GP, finishing 2nd as #6: black number on a white roundel on the tail sides and top, and on the nose top. Phil Hill was 3rd with fastest lap at the Italian GP at Monza as #18 (his first 246 start). At Morocco he was #4. Other Hawthorn 1958 numbers: Monaco #38, Dutch #5, French #4 (win), British #2, German #3, Italian #14.
246 F1.tobaccoNote: none - no tobacco (or any commercial) branding in this era; works Ferraris carried no sponsor decals on the bodywork. Tyre maker names appeared only on the tyre sidewalls. Englebert tyres.
246 F1.notes: Plain rosso corsa Dino 246 with no nose band at Morocco. Photos show black-on-white roundels throughout 1958.

Dino 156 F2.numberNote: German GP 1958, F2 class at the Nurburgring: Phil Hill was #23 (9th overall), a black number on a white roundel on the tail sides and on the nose top.
Dino 156 F2.tobaccoNote: none - no tobacco (or any commercial) branding in this era; works Ferraris carried no sponsor decals on the bodywork. Tyre maker names appeared only on the tyre sidewalls. Englebert tyres.
Dino 156 F2.notes: Plain rosso corsa. Small yellow shield on the scuttle sides, Borrani wire wheels.

256 F1.numberNote: Numbers were assigned per race by the organisers. Phil Hill 1959: French GP (Reims) #26, 2nd place (the number used here); Italian GP (Monza) #32, 2nd. 1960: Italian GP (Monza) #20, his win in the front-engined Dino 246. Period cars mostly had large white numerals painted straight onto the red nose top and body sides. The Ferrari museum car shows a black number on a white roundel, which some events used.
256 F1.tobaccoNote: none (no sponsor or tobacco branding in 1959-60; plain rosso corsa with a small yellow scudetto on the nose and scuttle side, and silver Borrani wire wheels).

156 F1.numberNote: Numbers were assigned per race. Phil Hill 1961: Italian GP (Monza, where he clinched the title) #2, the number used here. 1962: Dutch GP #1 (3rd place). Large white numerals were painted straight onto the red, on top of the sharknose and on the body sides behind the cockpit.
156 F1.tobaccoNote: none (1961-62 cars carried no sponsor names; Dunlop tyres and Shell fuel were not shown as body decals. The only marking is a small yellow scudetto on the nose tip and on the flank ahead of the cockpit. Wheels are silver Borrani wire wheels.)

156 F1-63.numberNote: Numbers were assigned per race. Surtees 1963: German GP (Nurburgring, his win) #7, the number used here; Dutch GP #2. White numerals were painted straight onto the red nose top and body sides. By mid-1963 the car ran light-coloured cast alloy wheels rather than wire wheels.
156 F1-63.tobaccoNote: none (no sponsor names on the bodywork; Dunlop tyres and Shell fuel only; small scudetto on the nose).

158 F1.numberNote: Numbers were assigned per race. Surtees 1964: Italian GP (Monza, his win in the red works car) #2, the number used here; German GP win #7; Mexican GP #7 (title decider). 1965: South African GP #1. Large white numerals were painted on the nose top and on the body side beside the cockpit. NART: at the 1964 US and Mexican GPs the car was entered by Luigi Chinetti's North American Racing Team in US colours (white with blue lengthwise stripes), in protest against the ACI/FIA. This entry describes the red works car used for the rest of 1964 and in 1965.
158 F1.tobaccoNote: none (no sponsor names on the body; Dunlop tyres and Shell fuel only). The red works car ran turquoise/pale-blue cast magnesium wheels, as seen on the Ferrari museum car and Surtees' own Goodwood car and described in model literature.

512 F1.numberNote: Surtees raced the flat-12 1512/512 F1 from the 1965 British GP onward. British GP (Silverstone, 3rd place, the car's best result) #1, the number used here; Italian GP 1965 #8. White numerals were painted on the nose top and body sides. In 1964 the 1512 ran in NART white/blue at Watkins Glen and Mexico (Bandini).
512 F1.tobaccoNote: none (same plain red works livery as the 158, with pale blue/turquoise magnesium wheels and no sponsor names).

312 F1-66.numberNote: Numbers were assigned per race. Surtees 1966: Belgian GP (Spa, pole, fastest lap and win) #6. White numerals were painted on the nose top and on the body side beside the cockpit. He left Ferrari in mid-1966.
312 F1-66.tobaccoNote: none (plain rosso corsa with no sponsor names; Dunlop tyres early in 1966, later Firestone; Shell fuel). Wheels are gold/bronze cast magnesium, as seen in a colour photo of the 1966 312 F1-66 at Monza. Later 1967 cars wore small Shell/Firestone/Magneti Marelli decals, but those are not used here.

stripes.note: thin white pinstripes along the cockpit rim and the upper and lower body/sidepod edges
white band around the top of the tall red airbox (green-white-red tricolore band in some photos), with a small scudetto

312 B3-74.numberNote: Fixed numbers: Lauda #12 in 1974. He also used #12 in the B3 at the first two races of 1975 (Argentina, Brazil). Black numerals sit on a white rounded-corner square on the sidepod sides and on the nose.
312 B3-74.tobaccoNote: none (no tobacco on the car. Lauda's personal Marlboro patch was on his helmet/overalls only. The car was all red with white pinstripes, not a white body. The white is only the rear wing top and the airbox band. No Fiat logos yet; they first appeared in 1977.)

stripes.note: Italian tricolour (green-white-red) stripe across the top of the white airbox
thin white pinstripe along the upper sidepod/body line

312 T.numberNote: Lauda #12 in 1975. He also raced the 312 T as reigning champion #1 at the first three 1976 rounds (Brazil, South Africa, US West). Black numerals on white panels with thin red outline, on the nose and on the airbox sides.
312 T.tobaccoNote: none. Aluminium wings are unpainted; 'Niki Lauda' was written in script on the cockpit side. FIAT box seen on the preserved car; Wikipedia's 312T article says Fiat logos first appeared in 1977, so FIAT may be a later addition (kept because it is on the preserved Lauda car).

stripes.note: green-white-red tricolore stripe running along each side of the cockpit, from the nose to the white roll-hoop fairing
white panel/pinstripe along the lower sidepod

312 T2.numberNote: Fixed numbers. Lauda #1 in 1976 (the car's main season) and #11 in 1977. Villeneuve #21 at his 1977 Ferrari debut races (Canada, Japan) and #12 in the T2 at the first two races of 1978 (Argentina, Brazil). Black numerals sit on the white nose-tip panel.
312 T2.tobaccoNote: none (no tobacco on the car. Marlboro was a personal helmet sponsor for Lauda and Villeneuve only.) The 1976 main-season car had no Fiat logo. Wikipedia says Fiat logos first appeared on a Ferrari F1 car on the 1977 T2B, so the 1977 Lauda #11 and Villeneuve #21 cars also carried a blue Fiat badge. Tyres were Goodyear in 1976-77; the T2s used at the start of 1978 ran on Michelin.

stripes.note: broad white band along the lower sidepod carrying the small sponsor stickers
white areas / pinstripe on the nose
white panel with black stripes on the engine cover behind the roll hoop

312 T3.numberNote: Villeneuve #12 in 1978 (and #12 in the T3 at Argentina/Brazil 1979). Scheckter #11 in the T3 at Argentina/Brazil 1979. Reutemann (not in our list) was #11 in 1978.

stripes.note: white rear section of the sidepod carrying the red race number, and a white band along the bottom of the sidepod/skirt carrying the small sponsor names
thin white pinstripe outlining the wide nose/wing-body edge

312 T4.numberNote: Fixed numbers in 1979: Scheckter #11 (world champion) and Villeneuve #12. White outlined numerals on the nose top. Red numerals on the white rear panel of each sidepod.
312 T4.tobaccoNote: none (no tobacco on the car; Marlboro appeared only on Villeneuve's helmet).

stripes.note: white rear section of the sidepod carrying the red race number, a white pinstripe along the sidepod top, and a white lower band with the small sponsor names
thin green-white-red tricolore line along the cockpit and engine-cover shoulder

312 T5.numberNote: Fixed numbers in 1980: Scheckter #1 (reigning champion), Villeneuve #2. White outlined numerals on the nose top. Red numerals on the white rear sidepod panel.

stripes.note: tricolour pinstripe running back from the cockpit side
thin white pinstripe along the lower sidepod

126 CK.numberNote: Villeneuve #27 (Pironi #28) in 1981. Large white numerals on the nose top; also on the Agip panel of the rear wing endplate.
126 CK.tobaccoNote: none (Marlboro did not appear on the Ferrari race cars until 1984)

stripes.note: tricolour pinstripe on the cockpit side

126 C2.numberNote: Villeneuve #27 (Pironi #28) in 1982; large white numerals on the nose top.

F1-89.numberNote: Fixed number for 1989: Mansell #27 (Berger #28). Large white number on the nose top just ahead of the front suspension, repeated in white on the black rear-wing endplates below a white Agip panel.
F1-89.tobaccoNote: Marlboro appeared only as a small white panel with red 'Marlboro' wordmark on the cockpit sides (under the driver's name) and a small one on the nose; there was no large tobacco graphic on the 1989 car. I found no evidence of it being removed at particular races, so it is shown for the whole season. The car's biggest graphics were Fiat (blue box on the engine cover), Agip (yellow badge on the sidepod) and Goodyear on the wings.

stripes.note: yellow flashes on the tips of the front-wing endplates and flaps
yellow flash at the top of the black rear-wing endplates, above the Agip box

F1-90.numberNote: Fixed numbers for 1990: Prost #1 (reigning champion), Mansell #2. White number on the nose top, repeated in white on the rear-wing endplates.
F1-90.tobaccoNote: Marlboro appeared only as small white panels with the red wordmark: on the cockpit sides (under the driver's name) and at the base of the nose ahead of the cockpit. This matches the Canadian GP photo and the GP Replicas and Amalgam replicas. I found no race where it was removed, so it is shown for the whole season.

stripes.note: yellow tips on the front-wing flaps and endplates
yellow flash at the top of the rear-wing endplates

F1-91.numberNote: Fixed number for 1991: Prost #27 (Alesi #28). White number on the nose top and on the rear-wing endplates. Prost drove the 642 for the first 6 rounds (USA to Mexico) and the 643 from the French GP to Japan. He was dropped before Australia, where Gianni Morbidelli drove car #27. The livery was essentially the same on both cars. This entry describes the 643, which ran at most of Prost's races (9 of 15).
F1-91.tobaccoNote: Marlboro appeared as a small white chevron ('roof') shaped panel with the red wordmark on the cockpit/engine-cover sides, plus small wordmarks on the nose. In the 1991 French GP photo the white chevron appears to carry no wordmark, so it may have been blanked at that race. The rest of the season used the wordmark, and that version is shown here.

stripes.note: white strip along the front-wing main plane carrying the Shell name

F310.numberNote: Fixed number for 1996: Schumacher #1 (reigning champion), Irvine #2. White number on the nose side near the tip, also on the rear-wing endplate. The car ran a low nose for rounds 1-7 and a raised nose from round 8.
F310.tobaccoNote: At most rounds there was a large white 'Marlboro' wordmark on the engine-cover sides (Imola 1996 photo), 'Marlboro' on a white panel on the rear-wing top flap, and a small wordmark on the cockpit side. At tobacco-restricted races the names became white 'barcode' bars: the German GP photo shows barcode stripes on the engine cover. McLaren likewise dropped Marlboro at France, Britain, Germany and the European GP, so the ban probably covered about 4 rounds. The wordmark version is shown because it ran at most races. Surviving museum cars (such as Beaulieu) wear the barcode version.

stripes.note: large white chevron ('Marlboro roof') panel on each side of the engine cover behind the airbox, carrying the red Marlboro wordmark
white chevron on the upper rear-wing flap
white strip along the front-wing main plane carrying the Shell name

F310 B.numberNote: Fixed number for 1997: Schumacher #5, Irvine #6 (Williams had #3/#4 after winning the 1996 constructors' title). Black number on the sidepod flank behind the Shell/Asprey logos and on the nose side.
F310 B.tobaccoNote: At most rounds the red 'Marlboro' wordmark sat in the white chevron on the engine-cover sides (Monza 1997 photo), with a white 'Marlboro' on the cockpit sides and the nose top. At tobacco-restricted races the chevron carried white 'barcode' bars instead: the German GP photo and RaceFans confirm this for 1997 Germany, and it probably also applied at France, Britain and the European GP, as with McLaren. The wordmark version is shown because it ran at most rounds.

stripes.note: white chevron ('Marlboro roof') panel on each side of the engine cover behind the airbox, carrying the red Marlboro wordmark

F300.numberNote: Fixed number for 1998: Schumacher #3, Irvine #4 (Williams #1/#2). Small black number on the nose side near the tip and on the rear-wing endplates.
F300.tobaccoNote: At most rounds there was a large white 'Marlboro' wordmark along the nose top, a red wordmark in the white chevron on the engine-cover sides, a black 'Marlboro' on the white upper rear wing, and a small wordmark on the cockpit side. At tobacco-restricted races (France, Britain, Germany and similar) the names were removed or replaced by barcode bars, which left the plain white chevron and white rear wing seen on the museum car. The wordmark version is shown because it ran at most rounds.

stripes.note: white lower strip on the black front wing carrying Shell

F399.numberNote: Schumacher #3 in 1999 (Irvine #4). Black-outlined white numeral on the nose top.
F399.tobaccoNote: Marlboro wordmark on the airbox sides and rear wing at most rounds; barcode/white panels at tobacco-restricted races (France, Britain, Germany), and 'Ferrari Formula One' replaced Marlboro at the 1999 Belgian GP. Chose the wordmark.

stripes.note: white chevron ('Marlboro roof') panel on each side of the engine cover behind the airbox, carrying the Marlboro wordmark
upper/trailing part of the rear-wing endplates white, continuing the white rear wing; lower part red with sponsor logos

F1-2000.numberNote: Fixed number for 2000: Schumacher #3, Barrichello #4 (McLaren #1/#2). Black number on the nose top ahead of the Shell pecten and on the rear-wing endplates.
F1-2000.tobaccoNote: At most rounds (Belgium 2000 photo; GP Replicas Suzuka model with its Marlboro sheet) there was a black 'Marlboro' across the white rear wing and in the white engine-cover chevron, plus white wordmarks on the nose top and cockpit side. At tobacco-restricted races (France, Britain, Germany and similar) these were blanked or replaced by barcode bars, and the white chevron and white rear wing stayed. The wordmark version is shown because it ran at most rounds.

stripes.note: white chevron ('Marlboro roof') panel on each side of the engine cover behind the airbox
upper part of the rear-wing endplates white, continuing the white rear wing; lower part red with Shell/Bridgestone/Magneti Marelli/GE

F2001.numberNote: Fixed number for 2001: Schumacher #1, Barrichello #2. Black number on the nose top and on the rear-wing endplates. Schumacher also raced an F2001 as #1 at the first two rounds of 2002 (Australia, which he won, and Malaysia) before the F2002 arrived. For those races the car carried Vodafone logos as the new title partner.
F2001.tobaccoNote: At most 2001 rounds there was a black 'Marlboro' across the white rear wing and in the white engine-cover chevron, plus white wordmarks on the nose top and cockpit side (GP Replicas Monaco 2001 model and its Marlboro decal sheet). At tobacco-restricted races (France, Britain, Germany and similar) these became barcode bars: a Commons photo of Schumacher in the F2001 shows barcode stripes across the rear wing. The wordmark version is shown because it ran at most rounds.

stripes.note: white Marlboro panel covering the engine-cover fin behind the airbox
white bargeboard/turning-vane wedge low on the sidepod leading edge with a thin red line

F2002.numberNote: Schumacher #1 in 2002 (from Brazil) and #1 again when the F2002 raced the first four rounds of 2003. Number shown in black on the top of the nose near the front suspension.
F2002.tobaccoNote: Marlboro wordmark on engine-cover fin and rear-wing top at most rounds; removed (plain white) at the British, French and United States GPs. Chose Marlboro version. Vodafone became major sponsor in 2002 (roundel on sidepods, wordmark on cockpit side and front-wing endplates).

stripes.note: large white Marlboro panel on the engine-cover fin behind the airbox
white bargeboard wedge low at the sidepod front with a red pinstripe

F2003-GA.numberNote: Schumacher #1 in 2003 (F2003-GA from the Spanish GP onwards).
F2003-GA.tobaccoNote: Marlboro wordmark on engine-cover fin and rear-wing top at most rounds; removed (plain white panels, as in the Silverstone photo) at the French, British and United States GPs. Chose Marlboro version. Olympus joined as a new sponsor in 2003 (small decals).

stripes.note: large white Marlboro panel on the engine-cover fin behind the airbox
white bargeboard wedge low at the sidepod front with a red pinstripe

F2004.tobaccoNote: Marlboro wordmark on engine-cover fin and rear-wing top at 14 of 18 rounds; removed (plain white panels, e.g. Indianapolis photo) at the Canadian, French, British and United States GPs. Chose Marlboro version. At Spa a 700th-GP logo was carried behind the seat and on the sidepods.

stripes.note: white Marlboro panel on the engine-cover fin behind the airbox
white bargeboard wedge low at the sidepod front

F2004 M.numberNote: Raced only at the 2005 Australian and Malaysian GPs; Schumacher #1.
F2004 M.tobaccoNote: Both of its races (Australia, Malaysia 2005) allowed tobacco branding: Marlboro wordmark on engine-cover fin and rear-wing top (as seen in Jerez testing photo).

stripes.note: large white Marlboro 'chevron' panel on the engine-cover fin behind the airbox
white strip along the nose top carrying the Marlboro wordmark
white bargeboard wedge low at the sidepod front with a red pinstripe

F2005.numberNote: Schumacher #1 all season (F2005 from Bahrain onwards).
F2005.tobaccoNote: Marlboro wordmark (black on white) on engine-cover fin, rear-wing top and nose top at 12 of 19 rounds; removed at the Canadian, United States, French, British, Turkish, Italian and Belgian GPs. Chose the Marlboro version (most rounds). Bahrain: black-tipped nose in mourning for Pope John Paul II.

stripes.note: white panel on the engine-cover fin behind the airbox (blank where Marlboro was banned)
row of red bars/teeth along the white rear-wing top in no-tobacco races
white barcode-like bars on the nose top ahead of the cockpit in no-tobacco races

248 F1.numberNote: Schumacher #5 (Massa #6); number in black on a white oval on the nose top.
248 F1.tobaccoNote: Marlboro wordmarks were shown only at 6 of 18 rounds (Bahrain, Malaysia, Australia, Monaco, China, Japan); removed at San Marino, Europe, Spain, Britain, Canada, USA, France, Germany, Hungary, Turkey, Italy and Brazil, where the white panels were left blank or carried red/white bars. Chose the no-wordmark version (most rounds, as in the Brazil photo).

stripes.note: white 'barcode' (vertical white bars on red) on the engine-cover fin behind the airbox
red barcode bars across the white rear-wing top
thin white pinstripes low along the sidepod flanks

F2007.tobaccoNote: Red/white barcode on engine-cover fin and rear-wing top at most rounds; actual Marlboro wordmarks only at Bahrain, Monaco and China. Chose the barcode version. Vodafone had left for McLaren; noticeably less white than 2000-06.

stripes.note: white panel on the engine-cover fin with red vertical 'barcode' bars
red barcode bars across the white rear-wing top

F2008.tobaccoNote: Barcode only (white/red bars on engine-cover fin and rear-wing top) at every round; per Wikipedia the Marlboro name was never shown in a 2008 race. Etihad Airways on the back of the rear wing; small Martini logos (blanked in France).

stripes.note: white barcode panel (red vertical bars, more Marlboro-chevron shaped) on the engine-cover fin
red barcode bars across the white rear-wing top

F60.numberNote: Raikkonen #4 (Massa #3); white number on the nose top.
F60.tobaccoNote: Barcode on engine-cover fin and rear-wing top at all rounds (2009 pattern evolved to look more like the Marlboro chevron); no Marlboro wordmark.

stripes.note: large white panel on the engine-cover fin; carried a red/white/black barcode at the first four rounds, a plain white rectangle from Spain onwards

F10.numberNote: Alonso #8 (Massa #7); white number on the nose top.
F10.tobaccoNote: Barcode on the engine cover only at the first four rounds (Bahrain, Australia, Malaysia, China); removed from the Spanish GP onwards and replaced by a plain white rectangle. Chose the plain-white version (15 of 19 rounds). Santander (new partner) on rear wing.

stripes.note: lower half of each rear wing endplate red (AMD / TATA / ferrari.com area), upper half white (V-Power / Santander)
white swept triangular panel on the engine-cover flank behind the airbox carrying the 'Scuderia Ferrari' logo (replaced the Marlboro barcode)

Ferrari 150° Italia.numberNote: Small white #5 near the nose tip; Massa #6. Numbers were very small in this era.
Ferrari 150° Italia.tobaccoNote: none visible. Philip Morris still sponsored the team (entered as 'Scuderia Ferrari Marlboro' for rounds 1-8, then 'Scuderia Ferrari'), but the 2010 white barcode was dropped and replaced by the white 'Scuderia Ferrari' logo panel on the engine cover, so no tobacco-derived marks on the car all season. Chose: no tobacco decal.

stripes.note: lower part of each rear wing endplate red (AMD / Mahle / ferrari.com), upper part white (V-Power / Santander)
white swept triangular panel on the engine-cover flank carrying the 'Scuderia Ferrari' logo

F2012.numberNote: White #5 on the top of the stepped nose near the tip; Massa #6.
F2012.tobaccoNote: none. Philip Morris remained a (hidden) partner but no Marlboro wordmark, chevron or barcode appeared on the car; chose plain design all season.

SF90.numberNote: Large white digits with black outline on the nose (upper side) and white on the black shark-fin panel of the engine cover.
SF90.tobaccoNote: Philip Morris 'Mission Winnow' (black wordmark on rear wing, front wing endplates and nose/cockpit side, plus a black slashed 'MW' graphic on the engine cover fin) ran at only 10 of 21 rounds (Bahrain-Monaco, rounds 2-6, and Japan-Abu Dhabi, rounds 17-21). At 11 rounds (Australia, and Canada through Russia) it was replaced by Ferrari's black '90 Years' anniversary logo. Chose the majority no-Mission-Winnow spec with the '90 Years' logo (as on Leclerc's car at Austria 2019).

SF1000.numberNote: White digits on the engine cover (the SF90's black engine-cover panel was deleted and the number moved there) and white on the nose top.
SF1000.tobaccoNote: Launched and tested with black 'Mission Winnow' wordmarks (rear wing mainplane, front wing endplates) and a black 'MW' graphic on the engine cover, but Mission Winnow appeared at none of the 17 races of 2020 (removed after a Codacons complaint in Italy); the rear wing top raced plain red. Chose the no-tobacco race spec. The burgundy 1000th-GP livery at Mugello (Tuscan GP) was a one-off and is not described here.

Entered as Scuderia (Ferrari) Mission Winnow at 13 of 22 rounds (1-6, Russia, and USA-Abu Dhabi); logos removed at 9 rounds (France to Italy, plus Turkey). ascari.notes: No overalls: a short-sleeved collared polo shirt in his 'lucky' light blue, worn with blue trousers (the legs accent here is the trouser colour), plus his light blue helmet. Motor Sport's article on his personal effects names the 'lucky blue polo shirt' and 'lucky blue trousers', and Motor Sport also calls blue shirts his signature. A 1953 Zandvoort winner's photo (black and white) shows the collared, buttoned polo. No sponsor patches. The shirt shade is a best estimate. The trouser shade is less certain: sources only say 'blue', so it may have been lighter or greyer. Confidence: high for the garment and light blue shirt, medium for the trouser shade.

fangio.notes: No overalls. Fangio raced in Suixtil clothing (an Argentine brand): short-sleeved shirts or polos with slacks, and the Suixtil name was sometimes on the slacks. El Grafico colour covers from 1954-55 show a pale blue short-sleeved button shirt with khaki or tan trousers. Another shows white trousers with a brown shirt. The legs accent here is the trouser colour. I found no dated colour photo from the 1956 Lancia-Ferrari season, so pale blue/white shirt with khaki trousers is taken from his typical outfit of 1954-57. Velocetoday also says he wore light blue trousers with white or yellow Suixtil polos in 1949. No team patches. Confidence: medium-low on the exact 1956 colours. The garment type is certain.

hawthorn.notes: His race 'uniform' was a dark green, waist-length zip windcheater jacket (Baracuta-style cotton; forum discussion suggests a Baracuta G35) over a white shirt with his trademark spotted bow tie, which earned him the French nickname 'Le Papillon'. He wore white trousers or white overalls below. The base colour is the green jacket. The collar accent is the white shirt collar and bow tie area, and the legs accent is the white trousers. No sponsor patches. Ferrari.com, formula1.com and an eyewitness at the 1958 Nurburgring (quoted on the Autosport Nostalgia Forum) all agree on green jacket, white shirt and bow tie. The bow tie was usually dark with white spots. Confidence: high for the jacket, shirt and bow tie. Medium for the exact green and for the trousers.

phil_hill.notes: Light blue ('azzurro') cotton overalls: one piece with a stand collar, breast pocket and belt, and a small embroidered Dunlop logo on the chest and hip (Ferrari ran Dunlop tyres). Motor Sport and period discussion say Ferrari drivers and mechanics of the 1950s-60s wore this light blue, and GPHelmet's 1961 replica is pale blue Dunlop overalls. I found no dated 1961 colour photo to confirm this myself; the Commons photos from 1961 Zandvoort are black and white and show only the helmet. Confidence: medium.

surtees.notes: Light blue cotton overalls, probably Les Leston, with an embroidered Dunlop logo above the breast pocket. Motor Sport names Surtees as one of the Ferrari drivers 'synonymous with blue overalls'. A Bonhams lot (Surtees's own Les Leston two-piece overalls, embroidered 'World Champion 1964', worn in 1965) confirms the maker and the Dunlop logos, but its text gives no colour. For the last two races (Watkins Glen and Mexico) the car ran in NART blue and white; there is no evidence he changed overalls for them. He often wore a dark quilted jacket over them in the paddock. Confidence: medium.

lauda.notes: Red fireproof Nomex overalls with a red collar. On the chest are yellow Ferrari shield and Agip patches, a Heuer shield, a Goodyear patch and a name patch. The colour photo from the 1975 Italian GP podium (title win) shows an all-red suit with yellow patches on the chest and no white panels. The 'Rush' costume, an OMP red suit labelled 'Niki Lauda Ferrari 1975', carries Ferrari, Goodyear, Heuer and Agip logos. Replicas of his 1976 suit add white shoulder and arm bands and a Parmalat patch; those belong to 1976, not 1975. Motor Sport says Lauda was also linked with Ferrari blue overalls, probably from 1974 or testing. Confidence: medium-high for red, medium for the patch list.

gilles_villeneuve.notes: He wore two different suits in 1979. From the French GP at Dijon (the famous duel with Arnoux) to the end of the season, including Zandvoort, Monza and his Watkins Glen win, he raced in a new white/silver Simpson Nomex suit, which only came in white. Motorsport.com reports this, and Peter Windsor saw him in 'a brand new pair of silver Simpsons' at a 1979 Fiorano test. Before France (Kyalami and Long Beach wins, Zolder, Monaco) he wore a red suit (about #d0312d) with white stripes down the arms and legs; a Zolder 1979 parade photo shows it. Patches on both suits: a Marlboro World Championship Team chevron, Michelin, Champion, Agip, a Ferrari shield, Heuer, his personal sponsors Giacobazzi and Smeg in large letters on the chest, Labatt on the shoulder and back, and his embroidered name. Base colour is set to white for the Dijon-to-Watkins Glen part of the season. Confidence: medium on which suit to show, since it changed mid-season.

scheckter.notes: Not red. Early in 1979 he wore suits in the colours of his personal sponsor, Brooklyn chewing gum. Peter Windsor saw 'blue Brooklyn chewing gum overalls' at a spring test. The dated colour photo from the 1979 Monaco GP (a race he won) shows a white suit with a red diagonal band across the chest, 'Brooklyn Chewing Gum' in dark navy letters, a Ferrari shield and an Agip patch. From mid-season he switched to the same white Simpson Nomex suit as Villeneuve and wore it for the rest of the year, including the title-winning Monza race (Motorsport.com). The red chest band does not fit any allowed accent area, so accents are empty. Confidence: medium-high for white, medium for the exact details.

mansell.notes: Plain red OMP Nomex overalls with fine white quilting stitch lines and white knitted cuffs. There are no white panels, and no Marlboro chevron panel on the suit itself. Chest patches: a white Marlboro chevron-logo patch with the name above it on the right breast, and Ferrari shield, Agip and Goodyear on the left. There are small Marlboro patches on both upper arms, Marlboro across the back, and a red belt with his name and Union Jack. A Bonhams lot of his 1989 OMP suit lists Marlboro, Goodyear and Agip patches. His 1990 Estoril suit, in red Nomex III, has the same layout. Confidence: high.

prost.notes: The same style as Mansell's: plain red Nomex overalls with white quilting stitch lines, white cuffs and no white body panels. On the right chest is a white 'A. PROST / Marlboro World Championship Team' chevron patch; on the left are Ferrari shield, Agip and Goodyear patches. There are Marlboro patches on both upper arms and Marlboro on the back, and a red belt with 'Alain Prost' and the French flag. Mansell's 1990 race-worn OMP suit (Bonhams) confirms the red suit and the Ferrari, Marlboro, Agip and Goodyear patches; Prost's own layout comes from GPHelmet's replica. Confidence: high.

michael_schumacher.notes: Red OMP suit with a fine white quilting grid. Its main feature is a large white Marlboro chevron panel across the mid-chest. The Marlboro wordmark appeared where tobacco advertising was allowed; elsewhere the white chevron shape stayed with the wording removed. Upper chest: Vodafone, Shell, Bridgestone and a Ferrari shield with Marlboro. I did not confirm the sponsor logos on the arms. There is a white Marlboro box on the back, and his name and German flag at the waist. RM Sotheby's sold a 2004 Hungarian GP OMP suit, but the lot text gives no colours; the layout comes from a replica image. The white chest chevron does not fit any allowed accent area, so accents are empty. Confidence: medium-high.

raikkonen.notes: Red Puma suit, with Puma supplying the team from 2007, and diamond quilting. White panels run down the sides of the torso and outer legs and along the underside of the arms, edged with thin white lines around the shoulders. On the chest: Shell and Bridgestone patches, a Ferrari shield with a thin green/white/red stripe running down from it, and small Marlboro logos on the chest and collar. Marlboro is on the upper back, and his name and Finnish flag are at the waist. The 2007 Brazil GP winner's photo shows the white underside of his sleeve when he waves. The design comes from a 2008 replica and a forum description ('the bit around Kimi's shoulder with the white outline'); the 2007 suit may differ slightly. Confidence: medium-high.

alonso.notes: Red Puma suit with white panels down the torso sides and under the arms. A white band across the chest carries the red Santander logo. Upper chest: Shell and UPS patches (UPS may be a 2013 addition; not confirmed for 2012) and a white Scuderia Ferrari shield. A thin green/white/red stripe runs down the sides of the legs. Kaspersky is on the shoulders, with his name and Spanish flag at the waist. I did not find a dated 2012 suit photo or auction text; this is taken from 2011 and 2013 replicas of the same design family, so small details may differ. Confidence: medium.

vettel.notes: Ferrari red Puma suit with white panels on the sides of the torso and the inner arms. Thin white stripes run over the shoulders (Kaspersky shoulder band), and white/red/green pinstripes run down the legs. There is a yellow Prancing Horse shield on the left chest and top of the back, and Shell and UPS patches on the right chest. The arms carry Ray-Ban, Hublot, Weichai, Singha, Alfa Romeo, Pirelli and Lenovo. His name and German flag are at the waist, with a circled 5 on the left leg. The chest had no big sponsor panel, since Santander had left. Mission Winnow branding appeared only from the Japanese GP in October. HOF Collection sold a race-worn 2018 suit and describes it this way. Confidence: high.

sainz.notes: Red Puma suit with a black shoulder yoke and black upper arms, and one thin white horizontal stripe across the chest. Shell and V-Power (VELAS) are on the right chest, Santander and Ceva on the left, with a yellow Ferrari shield at the collar. Snapdragon, AWS, Palantir and Richard Mille are on the arms. Other patches include #essereFerrari, and his name and flag are at the waist. In Sainz's own words at the 2024 suit launch, 'the black is gone', which confirms that 2022-23 suits used black. Confidence: high.

leclerc.notes: An all-red Puma suit with no black. Paired thin white and Giallo Modena yellow pinstripes form a U-shaped yoke across the chest and shoulders, run down the outer arms and down the legs. Both accents are really the same white and yellow pair: the shoulders accent is white and the legs accent is yellow. Shell and VGW Play are on the right chest, Santander and Ceva on the left, with a yellow Ferrari shield. The arms carry DXC Technology, AWS, Richard Mille, Peroni and others. His name is in white with number 16 at the waist. Special one-off suits were worn in a few races: an azzurro-blue-themed suit for Miami and a black, carbon-fibre-themed suit for Monza. Confidence: high.

hamilton.notes: Red Puma suit, a slightly deeper red than 2024, with 'sleek white lines' (Puma's words). A white line runs across the upper chest and shoulders, and there are white bands above the red knitted cuffs. Large blue-and-white HP roundels are on the chest and stomach; Shell and VGW Play are on the right chest, and UniCredit, Ceva, IBM and a yellow Ferrari shield are also on the chest. DXC Technology, Ray-Ban, AWS, Pirelli and Richard Mille are on the arms. His name and number 44 with a Union Jack are at the waist, and his name is on the back. One-off suits: all-white at Miami, a 1975 Lauda-style tribute at Monza and a special Las Vegas suit. Confidence: high for the season suit; exact line placement is from the replica image.
